# `Html.Unsafe`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Html.Unsafe — the trusted-HTML / inline-script escape hatch.

This submodule is the one home for the raw-HTML and inline-`<script>`
injection surfaces. Importing it discloses the `unsafe` capability
program-wide, so a dependency's raw sink is visible before the program runs.
The safe default is `Html.text`, escaped by construction; `unsafeRaw` and
`unsafeScript` bypass that escaping for trusted, verbatim content only.

Each member is a point-free `Kernel.kernel "Html_*"` alias to a retained kernel
(runtime: `ipe_runtime::ui::helpers::html_raw_node_` /
`html_script_node_`). The render sink emits the body verbatim, so the caller
owns the XSS / code-injection invariant: the input must be trusted,
author-controlled content.

## `unsafeRaw`

```ipe
unsafeRaw : String -> Html msg
```

`unsafeRaw s` — an UN-escaped raw HTML node. The `unsafe` prefix names the
XSS risk at every call site; user content goes through `Html.text` instead.
Framed content in raw markup is the author's to sandbox: the runtime fences
a frame in raw markup a patch carries, never one in the first paint.

## `unsafeScript`

```ipe
unsafeScript : String -> Html msg
```

`unsafeScript body` — an inline `<script>` element whose JavaScript body is
emitted VERBATIM. A script body is trusted-code injection: there is no
escaping it admits (escaping would corrupt the JavaScript, and the body runs
as code regardless), so the `unsafe` prefix names the risk and the body must
be trusted, author-controlled code. The kernel neutralises a literal
`</script` breakout at construction; the caller owns everything else.
